# Secondary tabs — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for secondary tabs when a section of a screen has several views of one thing and they belong below, not at the top: a record's overview, activity and settings. They are the second level — primary navigation says where you are, secondary tabs say which part of it you are looking at. The tabs come as data, including their content, so the whole set is one declaration. If the panels are different places with their own URLs, they are navigation and not tabs.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use inside content areas to separate related sub-sections.
- Mount only the active panel — hidden panels still announce.

**Don't**

- Don't use at the top level — that is primary tabs.
- Don't leave all tabs disabled — the component renders nothing rather than an empty tablist.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active indicator | resting | comp.secondary-tab.active-indicator | primary, 2px (not 3px) |
| Active label | resting | comp.secondary-tab.active-label | on-surface (not primary) |

### FAQ

**Why is the active text not primary?**

Per M3, secondary tabs mark selection with position (the 2px indicator), not color — the active label stays on-surface.

## Native

### Features

Reach for secondary tabs when a section has its own facets and a second level is clearer than a longer first one: the settings page of one feature, the views within one report. The data shape is identical to `Tabs` — `value`, `label`, optional `content` — so moving a tab between the two rows is a placement decision rather than a rewrite. The difference is the emphasis and where it sits: a secondary row belongs UNDER a primary one, marking subdivisions of the section the primary tab already chose. Two rows of tabs of equal weight is a hierarchy that says nothing.
